options.text: A prompt you send a few times in a row until the answer comes out right.
options.explanation: Sending a prompt again is a retry. Few-shot is about examples inside the prompt.

options.text: A prompt that includes a few examples of input and the output you want.
options.explanation: Right. A prompt with no examples is called zero-shot.

options.text: A very short prompt of only a few words, with no extra detail or context.
options.explanation: Length is not what the name means. Few-shot means the prompt holds a few examples.

questions.prompt: All your example replies are to happy customers. What is the risk?

options.text: The model may reply to unhappy customers in the same happy style.
options.explanation: Right. Examples that don't vary can teach a pattern you did not intend.

options.text: There is no risk. The model ignores the mood of examples and only copies their format.
options.explanation: Examples steer tone as well as format. Anthropic's guide names format, tone and structure.

options.text: The model will refuse to answer any review that is not happy.
options.explanation: It will still answer. The problem is that the answer may have the wrong tone.

questions.prompt: What does Gemini's guide say can happen with too many examples?

options.text: The model may overfit: it copies the examples too closely.
options.explanation: Right. Start with a few examples and test.

options.text: Nothing. More examples always make the answer better and more consistent.
options.explanation: The guide warns that too many examples can make the model overfit.

options.text: The model stops reading your instructions completely.
options.explanation: The guide does not say that. Its warning is about overfitting to the examples.
